latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 0991V
Sunrise Resources Plc
17 September 2026
17 September 2026
SUNRISE RESOURCES plc
(“Sunrise” or the “Company”)
Fundraising and Restoration of Trading
Director/PDMR Holdings
Further to its announcement of 9 September 2026, when the Company entered a Capital Access Window trading halt, Sunrise Resources plc (AIM: SRES), wishes to announce that it has conditionally raised £320,000 before expenses (“the Placing”) through the issue of 2,133,333,330 new Ordinary Shares of 0.001p each (the "Placing Shares”) at the price of 0.015 pence per Placing Share (the “Placing Price”).
The issue of the Placing Shares is conditional only on their admission to trading on AIM (“Admission”).
The Placing was arranged through the Company’s broker, AlbR Capital Limited (“AlbR”).
Each Placing Share will be issued with one warrant (the “Placing Warrants”) which will entitle the holder to apply for one new Ordinary Share in the capital of the Company at a price of 0.0175 pence per share at any time within 12 months from the date of issue. Should the average closing mid-market price of the Company's Ordinary Shares on AIM be equal to or greater than 0.0225 pence for five consecutive trading days from the date of issue of the Placing Warrants, the Company has the option to serve notice on the warrant holders to exercise the Placing Warrants and any Placing Warrants remaining unexercised after seven calendar days following the issue of such notice will be cancelled.
The issue of the Placing Shares is subject to Shareholder approval and a Shareholder Circular and a Notice of General Meeting will be issued in due course.
Following this announcement, the Capital Access Window has now closed and trading in the Company's Ordinary Shares on AIM will resume at 7:30 a.m. on 17 September 2026.
Directors Participation
Mr Patrick Cheetham, Executive Chairman of the Company, and Mr Adam Hainsworth, a non-executive director of the Company, have participated in the Placing and have subscribed £15,000 for 100,000,000 Placing Shares and £20,000 for 133,333,333 Placing Shares respectively. Their interests in the capital of the Company following Admission is as shown in the following table:

Use of Proceeds
The net funds raised pursuant to the Placing will be applied to general working capital and to advance the Company’s preparatory work for drill testing of various gold and base metal projects held in Nevada, USA and Australia. This includes geophysical exploration at the Reese Ridge and Lake projects in Nevada, USA.
Admission
Application is being made for the Placing Shares, which will rank pari passu with all existing Ordinary Shares, to be admitted to trading on AIM and Admission is expected to occur on or around 23 September 2026.

The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in Treasury. company_30s.what_they_do: SRES.L is a junior mineral exploration company that focuses on gold, copper, zinc and silver projects across the UK and the US.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits on several licences that cover large tracts of potentially resource‑rich land. If the company turns any of those tranches into a proven deposit, it could unlock a sizeable valuation jump for a small, low‑capital player in a commodity that is in steady demand from industry and technology.
company_30s.current_state: SRES.L is still in the exploration phase – no revenue, heavy cash burn, and a portfolio of licences rather than proven assets. The latest half‑yearly report shows modest capital expenditures and no cash flow, so the stock is trading near the bottom of a steep decline.

rns_narrative: The company has recently secured a prospecting licence for Bakers Gold, signed a heritage agreement that could unlock a gold‑rich zone, and announced a new copper‑silver‑gold project in Nevada. These moves suggest a strategy of expanding the geographic footprint and adding potentially high‑grade targets.

At the same time, there have been corporate governance updates – a new auditor and a revised corporate strategy – indicating the board is tightening controls and preparing for a possible funding round.
The company’s focus remains on exploration; no production or resource estimates have been released, so the market is still waiting for a first‑hand confirmation of value.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet skepticism – traders are watching but not buying.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: None – no bullish chatter has surfaced yet, which is typical for a company that hasn’t produced any resource data.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the lack of proven assets, high cash burn, and the fact that the company’s last update was only a licence grant, not a discovery.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The narrative is flat. There is no noticeable shift toward optimism or panic; the community is simply idle, waiting for the next announcement.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is dead, meaning the market has no built‑in narrative to keep the price anchored. If a catalyst hits, the stock could move sharply.

near_term_catalysts: A formal resource estimate or drill result from the Bakers Gold Heritage zone.
A financing announcement or equity placement that would provide the cash to start drilling in Nevada.
A significant price move in copper or gold that would make the company’s projects more attractive to investors.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden jump in trading volume, a spike in the stock’s volatility index, or a press release announcing a discovery. Any of these would signal that the market is re‑evaluating the company’s prospects.
expect_next.timing_regime: SRES.L appears to be in the early, very low‑confidence stage of a potential crash‑recovery cycle. The absence of a clear signal colour and the lack of any recent positive data suggest that the mean‑reversion, if it occurs, will be slow and will require a catalyst to trigger a move.

buy_vs_sell.lean: Neutral – the data does not yet support a contrarian bullish stance.
buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company produces a resource estimate that shows a modest deposit, the stock could double or triple, matching the typical 40‑50% return seen in green‑colour signals. The upside would be the difference between the current price and the midpoint of the 52‑week range.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: Without a discovery, the company’s cash burn will continue to erode value, and the stock could fall further into the deep‑crash territory. The worst case is a continued decline to a new low, potentially triggering a delisting if the company fails to raise capital.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is modest (≈+40%) but the downside is significant (≈-70% if the company fails to raise funds). The asymmetry is therefore not attractive for a contrarian trade.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter only if a resource estimate is announced and the price breaks above the 200‑day simple moving average. Use a 10‑% position sizing rule and set a stop 15% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike of at least 200% over the 10‑day average or a funding announcement. The trigger price would be the current price plus 5% to capture a potential rally.
playbook.if_passing: None – no terminal risk such as delisting has been identified, so the setup remains viable for a contrarian view if a catalyst appears.

ai_insights.bottom_line: SRES.L is a very early‑stage exploration company with no proven assets. While a discovery could create a sizeable upside, the current lack of signal and high risk make it a neutral play until a catalyst materialises.
